An APDK cross-sectional survey of 482 persons with disabilities in Nairobi's 11 sub-counties, fieldwork 2021, found 23.4% had used digital government services and reported inaccessible websites among the barriers.

KBC reports ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo saying the ministry is rolling out the Accessibility Standard for Digital Products, which he says is already influencing how services are designed and delivered.
The Grassroots Disability Agenda report calls for operationalisation of existing legal rights to accessible information and communication technologies in Kenya.

The National Assembly passed the Public Participation Bill, 2025 on 12 August 2026, awaiting presidential assent, requiring authorities to state how they will make participation accessible to persons with disabilities and provide translation and sign language services.
